summary: A worker-placement game where each worker type (raiders, horses, etc.) resolves differently based on a die roll, sending you around the board collecting resources to fulfill contracts and build up your tribe. It plays like a lighter cousin of Phillips' North Sea/West Kingdom games, with the same contract-fulfillment engine and a Mongol-steppe reskin.
criticised: Very similar to Phillips' other Garphill games, feels derivative
Dice mitigation can feel swingy for some workers

interaction.detail: Players occupy shared action spaces so there is some blocking and racing for key contract tiles, but most of the game is building your own tableau and fulfilling your own contracts. The shared board state (available spaces, contract tiles) is the main point of contact between players.

scoring.why: Final score sums contract rewards, trophies, gold, favor track position, and building bonuses collected across the campaign of worker-placement turns.
scoring.how_you_win: You fulfill contracts and complete quests using resources gathered through worker placement and dice rolling, banking VP from many different sources; the player with the most points at game end wins.
